items.claim: The 24:3-4 house-building figure is accurately grounded: both quotes collate at byte tier and the verses share a genuine wisdom-instrument vocabulary.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.24.3 בְּ֭חָכְמָה יִבָּ֣נֶה בָּ֑יִת and oshb:Prov.24.4 חֲדָרִ֣ים both collate BYTE against their cited verses. The pair forms an instrumental tricolon spanning 24:3-4 (בְּ֭חָכְמָה / וּ֝בִתְבוּנָ֗ה / וּ֭בְדַעַת -- wisdom/understanding/knowledge), and the verses carry no adversative vav-contrast, matching the row's declarative (non-antithetic) parallelism-class label.

items.claim: The rejected_alternative's claim that no building-vocabulary token repeats past verse 4 overlooks an undisclosed wisdom-term recurrence at the row's own seam.
items.evidence: 24:4's וּ֭בְדַעַת and 24:5's דַּ֝֗עַת share the root dalet-ayin-tav (Hebrew ד-ע-ת, 'knowledge'): the bare 24:5 form collates at SKELETON tier (not byte/accent_stripped) against the 24:4 window -- a genuine consonantal-root match via the ordinary vav+bet prefix on the 24:4 token, not a hazard-class contained-substring collision. This is the third term of 24:3-4's own wisdom-triad (בְּ֭חָכְמָה / וּ֝בִתְבוּנָ֗ה / וּ֭בְדַעַת), so its reappearance in 24:5's וְאִֽישׁ דַּ֝֗עַת is exactly the kind of byte-true device the cross-seam-cohesion rule requires disclosing before the pair is treated as an unconnected cluster; the row's own device_notes independently label both 24:3-4 and 24:5-6 as wisdom's-benefit clusters, underscoring the missed link.

items.claim: The scheme-root catchword binding 24:8 to 24:9 is byte-verified and correctly named.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.24.8 (מְחַשֵּׁ֥ב לְהָרֵ֑עַ; מְזִמּ֥וֹת) and oshb:Prov.24.9 (זִמַּ֣ת אִוֶּ֣לֶת) all collate BYTE; מְזִמּ֥וֹת and זִמַּ֣ת share the root z-m-m (Hebrew ז-מ-ם), verified directly in the byte text at the verse-8/verse-9 seam, matching the row's catchword claim.

items.claim: The imperative-plus-rebutted-excuse reading of 24:11-12 is grounded, and the ellipsis-joined 24:12 quote still collates at byte tier in both halves without misrepresenting the verse.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.24.11 (הַ֭צֵּל לְקֻחִ֣ים לַמָּ֑וֶת) collates BYTE. The 24:12 quote is spliced across an ellipsis (תֹאמַ֗ר...הֲֽלֹא); each half re-collates BYTE independently against oshb:Prov.24.12, and the full verse text (כִּֽי תֹאמַ֗ר הֵן֮ לֹא יָדַ֪עְנ֫וּ זֶ֥ה הֲֽלֹא תֹ֘כֵ֤ן לִבּ֨וֹת הֽוּא יָבִ֗ין וְנֹצֵ֣ר נַ֭פְשְׁךָ ה֣וּא יֵדָ֑ע וְהֵשִׁ֖יב לְאָדָ֣ם כְּפָעֳלֽוֹ) shows the skipped material is the quoted excuse itself, so the ellipsis fairly represents the verse's you-say/is-it-not-so structure.

items.claim: The vocative-reopening and hope-refrain claims are byte-grounded, and the 24:14 petuchah disclosure matches the pmarks inventory exactly.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.24.13 (אֱכָל בְּנִ֣י דְבַ֣שׁ) and oshb:Prov.24.14 (כֵּ֤ן דְּעֶ֥ה) collate BYTE. The clause וְ֝תִקְוָתְךָ֗ לֹ֣א תִכָּרֵֽת, quoted from 24:14, also collates at BYTE tier directly against oshb:Prov.23.18 (not merely accent_stripped), so the claimed exact-wording recurrence is fully byte-true. pmarks_Prov.json lists Prov.24.14 as PE only -- matching the row's disclosure, correctly labeled tier-3/single-witness and not conflated with the book's one SAMEKH (Prov.24.22, outside this row's span).

items.claim: The direct-address-plus-antithetic-motive reading of 24:15-16 is byte-grounded, and its 24:14 petuchah citation matches the pmarks inventory.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.24.15 (אַל תֶּאֱרֹ֣ב) and oshb:Prov.24.16 (כִּ֤י) collate BYTE; 24:16's צַדִּ֣יק...וָקָ֑ם / וּ֝רְשָׁעִ֗ים יִכָּשְׁל֥וּ is a genuine righteous/wicked antithesis, matching the row's parallelism-class label. The petuchah citation at Prov.24.14 matches pmarks_Prov.json (PE only), correctly labeled single-witness/tier-3.

items.claim: The row's characterization of 24:17 as opening a prohibition unrelated to the ambush warning just closed overlooks an undisclosed root recurrence from 24:16.
items.evidence: 24:16's יִפּ֣וֹל ('falls', root n-p-l / Hebrew נפל with the nun assimilated into the following consonant -- the standard I-Nun imperfect pattern, visible in the dagesh) and 24:17's own quoted בִּנְפֹ֣ל ('when...falls', infinitive construct, unassimilated נ-פ-ל) are the same root at immediately adjacent verses; both collate BYTE against their verses. This byte-true device straddles the row's own claimed seam and is not disclosed, contradicting the 'unrelated' characterization, though the formal genre split (ambush-warning vs. schadenfreude-prohibition) may still be defensible on other grounds. The row's ketiv/qere disclosure at 24:17 (אויביך/אֽ֭וֹיִבְךָ) is correct and matches pmarks_Prov.json's single K/Q note at Prov.24.17 -- that part of the mark-disclosure lens is compliant.

items.claim: The envy-root inclusio between 24:1 and 24:19 is real and closely byte-grounded, and the row correctly treats it as texture rather than a boundary-widening claim.
items.evidence: 24:19's quoted תְּ֝קַנֵּ֗א collates BYTE against its own verse; cross-checked against oshb:Prov.24.1, the corresponding תְּ֭קַנֵּא collates at ACCENT_STRIPPED tier -- identical consonants and vowel-points, differing only in verse-position-dependent cantillation, the strongest possible match across two separate verses. The row does not extend this into a boundary claim near the 24:22 SAMEKH / 24:23 gam-elleh header, correctly leaving the tier-3 parashah layer and the C3|C4 seam untouched by this span.
